label: Precise low-kick line with restrained workload
effort: Express a crisp low rotational kick along a preselected empty line and finish in a repeatable support position.
brief: The demand is controlling direction and stopping the leg without reducing every attempt to slow rehearsal. Supporting jobs cover a marked bilateral finish, a qualified single-leg turn, drop-step loading, a precise chamber stop and a crossover-to-base recovery. These are planned tasks, not additional reactive trials.
marker: valid E2 attempts out of four per leg that pass through the coach-defined empty directional window with a soft knee, active recoil and a two-second finish in the chosen stance.

e.name: Rotational jump to an offset stance gate
e.execution: Cones outside the landing area define a comfortable shallow split-stance finish, not an obstacle. From parallel feet, use one low rotational jump up to 45 degrees and land with the chosen support foot slightly ahead inside that gate. Hold 2 s.
e.job: Control the final two-foot arrangement after rotational force rather than simply completing an angle.
e.gate: Use a larger gate or smaller turn instead if targeting disrupts landing; never land on or jump toward a cone.
e.novelty: Planned spatial target and asymmetric landing base, unlike earlier unconstrained parallel rotational catches.

e.name: Low roundhouse through an empty direction gate
e.execution: The coach identifies an empty low kick line with cones placed outside the sweep and a visual height reference from outside reach. From a stationary rear-leg stance, kick through that line below hip height, keep the knee soft, recoil and recover. Nothing is struck.
e.job: Directly preserve hip-led acceleration while controlling the kick direction and recovery endpoint.
e.gate: Use a wider visual window or shorter arc instead if accuracy causes knee lockout or leaning; target accuracy alone is not a valid rep.
e.novelty: Accuracy-constrained full kick with a fixed empty window; a declared task variant, not measured impact practice.

e.name: Small single-leg turn hop to same-leg stick
e.execution: From the named leg, make one low hop with a small in-air turn, no more than 30 degrees, and land on that same foot already aligned with the pelvis. Hold 2 s. No travel goal or rebound.
e.job: Qualify control of rotational force on the leg that must remain the kick support.
e.gate: Only use the single-leg version after a controlled small unturned hop is known. Otherwise use instead a single-leg takeoff to a two-foot turning catch, same four flights; record four bilateral instead of unilateral landings.
e.novelty: Same-leg rotational flight/landing; earlier same-leg hops did not turn, and earlier turning flights landed on two feet.

e.name: Short drop-step lead-leg roundhouse
e.execution: The kicking leg begins in front. Take one small rear-foot drop step to load the support hip, turn that foot freely and deliver a low lead-leg roundhouse without another gather. Recoil into a comfortable split stance; stay within 2 m.
e.job: Use a compact rear-hip load to free the lead leg while retaining the planned kick line.
e.gate: Use a shallower drop step instead if the lead leg drags or the support knee twists; do not add speed and step length together.
e.novelty: Rear support-foot drop step precedes front-leg release; differs from the Class 2 no-step lead kick and the Class 9 retreat onto a new receiving leg.

e.name: Supported fast chamber lift to a fixed stop
e.execution: With fingertip support and the foot initially beneath the hip, accelerate the folded knee into a coach-selected low chamber height and stop it there for 2 s without overshooting. Lower slowly; no kick arc or band.
e.job: Practice cutting off free-thigh acceleration at the selected chamber, supporting a consistent low kick trajectory.
e.gate: Use a lower stop point instead if the pelvis tips or the leg overshoots; do not force end-range holds.
e.novelty: Endpoint-control constraint on a supported chamber lift, rather than maximizing lift speed or using a backward hover start; declared related variant.

e.name: Crossover recovery to a marked kick base
e.execution: From a slightly open stance, take one short crossover recovery step, then uncross the feet as the pelvis turns into a premarked comfortable kick base. Stop for 2 s with both feet supporting. No knee lift, kick or jump; path stays within 2 m.
e.job: Recover an exact useful two-foot base after reorientation, instead of leaving the feet crossed or too narrow.
e.gate: Use less crossover distance and a wider base instead if foot placement is inconsistent; do not force a fast turn while crossed.
e.novelty: Crossover recovery ending at a spatially defined two-foot base, not the earlier traveling crossover-to-chamber.

p_jobs: Maintain the main planted push while reserving attention for accurate explosive finishes.
Keep posterior-chain control without a second hinge round.
Maintain lateral/adductor support for the kick line and crossover recovery.
Preserve direct hip-turn strength with one controlled round after the precision drills.
Maintain active chamber strength at a reproducible height without adding a second round.
Keep ankle force and full heel travel with one challenging set.
s_jobs: Easy hip/foot strengthening reinforces repeatable alignment after the precision tasks; no extra balance challenge is added.
readiness: Precision is subordinate to a free support-foot turn and controlled knee. Do not assume single-leg rotation is earned by earlier written hops; use the two-foot catch unless that control is actually known. Cones and coach references stay outside all leg/landing paths.
strength_reason: Reduce Class 10 [1,1,1,2,1,1] to [1,1,1,1,1,1]: 76 working reps in 11 bouts. Keep the same challenging relative effort rather than chase fatigue before the final comparison class.
exposure_note: Eight landings by default: four bilateral gated catches plus four qualified same-leg turn landings. If E3 uses its two-foot catch, all eight landings are bilateral. Twenty grounded efforts include twelve kicks. Spatial misses remain attempts; there are no bonus target attempts.
space: Each stationary drill has full swept-leg clearance; moving footwork stays within 2 m plus 2 m recovery in one 10 m lane. Cones mark safe external boundaries and must not occupy landing spots. Bench fit and actual cone quantity remain practical checks.
progression: Class 10 introduced an early cue; Class 11 removes cue uncertainty and lowers strength volume while adding planned endpoint constraints. New precision conditions are separate tests, not proof of increased power or a license for narrower unsafe targets.
audit: Small targets that would force knee lockout or landing near cones were rejected. The single-leg turn is explicitly conditional with a same-dose two-foot catch. Precision variants are labeled honestly; they are not advertised as unrelated new movement families.
authoring_handoff: Review Class 11 and actual feedback, then finalize Class 12 with matched baseline comparisons only where useful, and complete the full-sequence audit before declaring the written curriculum complete.
current_handoff: Record actual delivery/response and review the next saved class against readiness.
